South Africa's bowling response was spearheaded by KA Maharaj (9/129), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Concluding at 338/10 (104.1 ov), Sri Lanka posted a competitive total, ensuring a closely matched contest.

Sri Lanka's bowling response was spearheaded by HMRKB Herath (6/98), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Dismissed for 290/10 (86.5 ov), South Africa succumbed to fourth-innings pressure as Sri Lanka's bowlers closed out the victory.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Sinhalese Sports Club Ground commenced with high tactical intensity as Sri Lanka posted 338/10 (104.1 ov) in their opening innings. In response, South Africa countered with 124/10 (34.5 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 9-Wicket Spell: KA Maharaj (9/129), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, KA Maharaj delivered a masterclass for South Africa (2 Runs & 13 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (Sri Lanka 55%) and allowing Sri Lanka to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, South Africa faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. Sri Lanka's bowling unit, bolstered by A Dananjaya (43 Runs & 7 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing Sri Lanka won by 199 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: Sri Lanka's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While South Africa produced fighting phases, Sri Lanka won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
